paper_metadata.title: Special Features of the Structure of Laser-Welded Joints of High-Temperature Alloys

evidence.quote: Atter welding with the chosen rates we observed, almost over the entire weld-penetration depth of the sheet forgings (excluding the place of formation of the gas-vapor channel ("dagger" penetration)), the formation of a structure consist- ing of columnar crystallites joining in the center at different angle.

attributes.morphology: dendritic, more dispersed with increasing welding rate

evidence.quote: Welding in all the investigated regimes was characterized by dendritic crystallization of the weldpool, which was deter- mined by the conditions of the appearance of concentration

As the welding rate was increased to v w = 130 m/h and higher, the welds began to acquire a wine- glass shape (Fig. 2). This can be explained as follows: with increase in welding rate, the volume source of heat that shapes the weld is changed to a linear source.

Atter welding with the chosen rates we observed, almost over the entire weld-penetration depth of the sheet forgings (excluding the place of formation of the gas-vapor channel ("dagger" penetration)), the formation of a structure consist- ing of columnar crystallites joining in the center at different angle.

Atter welding with the chosen rates we observed, almost over the entire weld-penetration depth of the sheet forgings (excluding the place of formation of the gas-vapor channel ("dagger" penetration)), the formation of a structure consist- ing of columnar crystallites joining in the center at different angle.

As a rule, with increase in the inclination of the dendrites to the axis of the welded joint the latter becomes more suscep- tible to the formation of hot cracks, because the number of elements of structural joints where intergrain slip is possi- ble decreases considerably [3].
Welding in all the investigated regimes was characterized by dendritic crystallization of the weldpool, which was deter- mined by the conditions of the appearance of concentration

We should also note the substantial segrega- tion inhomogeneity of the metal of the welded joints. In ac- cordance with the data of [2, 3] titanium and tungsten tend to a more intense segregation in the investigated alloys. Tita- nium enriches interaxial spacings and depletes the axes of dendrites.
